content: Google DeepMind shipped two new models on September 2, 2026: Gemini 3.8 Flash, an upgraded general-purpose “workhorse” model, and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a specialized variant built to find software vulnerabilities and write patches for them on its own. The pairing marks the third Flash release in six weeks, and it’s the first time Google has bundled a mainstream model launch with a dedicated cybersecurity model restricted to vetted governments and infrastructure operators, according to MarkTechPost. ... The announcement landed simultaneously across Google’s official channels and independent outlets. Google DeepMind’s own account described the release in a single post: “Two new Gemini models are here to help scale your AI agents and secure code: 3.8 Flash: our most intelligent model yet with significant gains from 3.7 Flash across software engineering, agentic tasks, and multi-step reasoning,” according to Google DeepMind’s post on X. The same post added a second line describing the security model: “3.8 Flash Cyber is our most capable cybersecurity model with frontier-level vulnerability detection and automated patching.” ... Google DeepMind CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu confirmed the timing directly, posting “Today we’re launching Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber and Gemini 3.8 Flash,” and describing the Cyber variant as “our most capable cybersecurity model for finding and fixing vulnerabilities,” according to his post on X. Coverage from Android Authority, Thurrott, and Investing.com all confirmed the same September 2 launch date, framing the story around the arrival of a government-focused security model rather than the general Flash update. ... Google DeepMind’s own leadership used the launch to frame both models as complementary tools for scaling AI work safely. content: Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 Scores 61 On Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, At Par With Grok 4.6 ... GPT 5.6 Sol ... After some time in the wilderness following the failure of Llama 4, Meta is firmly back in the AI race. ... Meta’s newly released Muse Spark 1.3 has scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, the benchmarking firm’s composite score built from evaluations spanning knowledge work, agentic tasks, coding, and scientific reasoning. The score puts Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh) in a tie with Grok 4.6 (high) and GPT-5.6 Sol (max), and just one point behind GPT-5.6 Sol (high fallback) and Claude Opus 5 (max), both at 63, and well within range of the current leader, Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback), at 66. ... Artificial Analysis’s chart places ten models in a tight band near the top. Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback) leads at 66, followed by Claude Opus 5 (max) at 63. Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh) then ties for third at 61 with GPT-5.6 Sol (max) and Grok 4.6 (high). Just below that sit Kimi K3 (max) and Z.AI’s GLM-5.3 (max), both at 60, followed by Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) at 59, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 (max) at 53, GPT-5.6 Luna (max) at 52, and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3 Ultra trailing at 38. ... The result puts Meta ahead of every Google model on the chart and effectively level with OpenAI and xAI’s current top offerings, a notable turnaround for a lab that was scoring in the low 50s as recently as August with Muse Spark 1.2.
